page.layout: One printed page (left of the scan). Running head at top. Running text in one column, with margin notes in the left margin. Neighbouring page edge at right, not transcribed.

main_text.p: furus[?] est ad Deum, nè talis affectus in animo ejus ingeneretur, non cum ad res bene gestas respicere Sermo jubet, sed recordari communium humana natura debitorum, quorum quivis prorsus particeps est; & rogare judicem, ut delictorum impunitatem largiatur. Hæc ille. De qua re eleganter sanè {o}Chrysostomus, Recte factorum certissimus thesaurus oblivio.Ad populum Antioch. Hom. 38.
main_text.head: Opinionem Meriti de Condigno ex necessitate & difficultate vera gratitudinis convincit falsitatis.
main_text.p: PRimò, Necessitas gratitudinis ex ingrati-tudinis atrocitate optimè elicitur. Ingratitudinis verò vitium apud Ethnicos ipsos adeò videbatur detestabile, ut Seneca rationem daturus, cur non hoc, sicut cætera vitia, in foro humano actionem inveniat, scitè & argutè, {*}Lib.3.de beneficiis, cap.6.Non quòd absolvimus, inquit, hoc invisum vitium: sed cùm difficilis esset incerta rei æstimatio, inter ea vitia reliquimus, quæ ad deos vindices mittimus. Sic ille de suis Ethnicis, qui inter id genus vitia paricidium numerat. Sed & ingratitudinis iniquitatem satis ostendit, adversus populum Judæ severa illa

page.notes: Left margin notes transcribed at their places: "o Ad populum Antioch. Hom. 38." beside the Chrysostomus line, and "* Lib.3.de beneficiis, cap.6." beside "argutè". The reference mark before Chrysostomus is a small square-like sign in the scan; I have read it as "o" to match the note. "furus" at the start of the page is doubtful (first letter could be an f-like or i-like form). Faint show-through from the reverse side and the neighbouring page edge are ignored. "Dei" at the lower right is treated as the catchword.
